title: Service JWT verifier tolerates absent iss/aud claims during rollout (token-confusion residual risk)
taxonomy: M1 — Broken authentication / token audience confusion
description: verifyServiceJwt enforces iss/aud only when the claims are PRESENT; a signature-valid token carrying neither iss nor aud is accepted (with a console.warn) to support a staged rollout (#1773/#1843). Because every RAG route authorizes off this same verifier and the signature is the only hard gate, any token minted with the RAG public key's private counterpart but WITHOUT iss/aud is accepted regardless of its intended audience. This is a genuine cross-service token-confusion weakening, but it is an explicitly documented, issue-tracked, rollout-gated exception with an inline justification, and the strict flip (hard-reject absence) is tracked in #1843. Per fp-rules (documented exception) it belongs in an accepted-risk appendix, not a headline. Residual exposure is realized only if the same signing key is reused by another ATC service that omits aud.
okWhen: A single dedicated RS256 signing key is used only by atc-main to mint RAG service tokens, so no other-audience token can be signed with the accepted key; and the #1843 strict flip lands once absent-claim warns reach zero in prod.
notOkWhen: The same SERVICE_JWT private key is (or becomes) shared with another service that mints tokens without an aud claim — those tokens would authenticate to the RAG service and inherit whatever tenant_id/service_identifier they carry.

title: rag_retrieval_log_daily RLS policy is USING(TRUE) — cross-tenant analytics exposed the instant any anon/authenticated grant is added
description: rag_retrieval_log_daily holds per-tenant retrieval request counts + latency aggregates (tenant_id, day, outcome). Its only SELECT policy is `USING (TRUE)` — every role that can reach the table sees every tenant's rows. Today this is NOT exploitable: I verified against the live RAG database that anon/authenticated/public hold ZERO table grants on this (and every other RAG table), so PostgREST denies them at the grant layer before RLS is evaluated (confirmed empty grantee set; RLS enabled). It is flagged as latent fragility, not a live leak: unlike the deny-all (zero-policy) tables, this permissive policy means the ONLY thing preventing cross-tenant exposure is the absence of a grant — one accidental `GRANT SELECT ... TO authenticated` (or a Supabase default-privilege change) turns it into a cross-tenant metadata leak with no second layer. rag_media_assets:51 has the same shape but is scope-filtered (global-or-own-tenant), so it degrades more gracefully.
okWhen: anon/authenticated hold no table-level grant on rag_retrieval_log_daily (verified true as of this review) — the grant layer is the effective control and the permissive policy never comes into play.
notOkWhen: A grant is ever added to anon or authenticated on this table (directly or via ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES): USING(TRUE) then returns every tenant's retrieval analytics to any holder of the project's anon key.
